extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational social science, network science, and machine learning studying information diffusion and building Bayesian mixture Hawkes models for social media cascades
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and evaluating a Bayesian Mixture Hawkes (BMH) hierarchical model that jointly learns source-, item-, and cascade-level influences on online content spread, and using it for cold-start popularity prediction, temporal-profile generalization, and counterfactual headline-style analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-start popularity prediction (ARE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Task: predict the popularity N_a* of an out-of-sample article a* using the trained publisher-level BMH-P model. Evaluation metric: Average Relative Error (ARE) over test articles, where ARE(a) = |(N̂_a - N_a) / N_a|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate expected cascade size per cascade class and average across cascade-feature empirical distribution; use Eq. (5) (ˆN_a* ≈ Ĉ_ρ · Σ_k z_{a*,c}^{α,k} · [1 + exp(δ_{a*,α,k} + γ_{α,k} · y_{a*})]^{-1} · f̂_ρ(x) summed over x). Report median and 25th/75th quantiles across articles; lower ARE is better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal-profile generalization (holdout log-likelihood / NLL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Task: evaluate how well the BMH-K model captures the inter-event (interarrival) time distribution of unseen cascades of unpublished articles. Metric: log-likelihood (negative log-likelihood reported as NLL or holdout log-likelihood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the log-likelihood of test interevent-time sequences under the trained BMH-K (L(P_Θ | {T_ac})). Use Eq. (8) for half-life predictions where needed. Report median and quantiles; higher log-likelihood (lower NLL) indicates better temporal generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model comparison to benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare BMH model performance against baselines and competing models: Dual Mixture Model (DMM), Empirical Bayes (EB), cascade-size regression (CR) models, and publisher-level joint Hawkes process (HP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate all methods on the same Fit/Test splits using the same metrics (ARE for popularity, holdout log-likelihood for temporal). Visualize and report medians and 25/75 quantiles (e.g., box/dot plots) to compare central tendency and spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separable Hawkes process modeling (µ = 0 for retweet cascades)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use separable Hawkes processes for cascades: conditional intensity λ(t) with branching factor α and memory kernel g(t; Θ); for Twitter retweet cascades assume µ = 0 so all retweets are offspring of the original tweet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit separability to split estimation into popularity (α) and kernel (Θ) subproblems (Eq. (1)). Use formulations that yield Borel-distributed cascade sizes for α estimation and interevent-time likelihood for Θ estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixture of separable Hawkes processes (BMH structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cascade groups using a hierarchical mixture: K_α popularity classes (branching factor α) and K_Θ kernel classes (Θ = [θ, d]), where each cascade's α and Θ are drawn from mixtures with membership probabilities influenced by features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMH divides into two independent submodels: BMH-P (popularity) and BMH-K (kernel). Learn both class centers (δ parameters) and membership logits (z expressions) using item- and cascade-level features (Eqs. (2)-(3), (6)-(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature role assumptions (which features affect what)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumptions: item-level features (y_a, e.g., headline embedding) influence the centers (location) and membership probabilities of popularity and kernel classes; cascade-level features (x_ac, e.g., seed user follower count) influence only the membership probabilities (not the class centers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely, in BMH-P logit(α_ac) = δ_{a,α,k} + γ_{α,k} · y_a and membership zac_{α,k} depends on β terms times x_ac and γ_zα,k times y_a (Eqs. (2)-(3)). In BMH-K y_a affects θ but not d for identifiability (Eq. (6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of kernel parametrization (power-law kernel preferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a power-law memory kernel g(t) = θ · d^θ · (t + d)^{-(1+θ)} for Hawkes processes, as it empirically outperforms alternatives for popularity prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate Θ = [θ, d] per cascade class; when using power-law kernel, compute derived quantities such as half-life τ_{1/2} = d · (2^{1/(2θ)} - 1?) (paper uses closed-form expression per chosen parametrization) and use it for temporal interpretation (Eq. (8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting number of mixture components (K_α, K_Θ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine K_α and K_Θ by fitting non-Bayesian mixtures first (DMM/KMM) and inspecting modality of fitted parameter distributions (e.g., bimodality in logit(α) suggests K_α = 2; trimodality in (log c, log θ) suggests K_Θ = 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit DMM/KMM across publishers with multiple EM initializations, examine distribution modes, and set hyperparameters K accordingly. Use informative priors in Bayesian fit to identify classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priors and identifiability (informative priors to identify classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Informative priors must be set on class-center parameters (e.g., δ_{α,k}, δ_{zα,k}, δ_{θ,k}, δ_{d,k}, δ_{zΘ,k}) to identify mixture classes in parameter space; weakly informative priors elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior locations guided by DMM/KMM fits (paper lists numeric priors in Supplement). Provide regularization where needed (Laplace priors for high-dim feature effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularization for high-dimensional item features (Laplace priors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Laplace (L1) priors on γ parameters that map item-level headline embeddings to class centers/membership (e.g., γ_{α,1}, γ_{α,2}, γ_{zα,2}, γ_{θ,2}, γ_{θ,3}, γ_{zΘ,2}, γ_{zΘ,3}) to impose sparsity/regularization given |y_a| = 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Laplace scale small enough to regularize but not to zero-out necessary signals; paper uses Laplace(0, 0.01) for many γ priors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-start prediction assumptions and marginalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Cold-start prediction marginalizes over unobserved cascade-level features x_ac for a new article: assume independence f_ρ(x | y) ≈ f_ρ(x) and approximate the expectation by summing over empirical follower-count distribution f̂_ρ(x); use Ĉ_ρ as estimated cascade count (average cascades per article) in final scaling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume cascade feature is 1D discrete nonnegative (e.g., follower count) to turn integrals into sums; set Ĉ_ρ from training data and compute ˆN_a* per Eq. (9) / Eq. (5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Half-life prediction and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Predict cascade half-life τ_{1/2} for an out-of-sample item using the BMH-K model and power-law kernel parameters via Eq. (8): ˆτ_{a*}^{1/2} ≈ Σ_k z_{a*,c}^{Θ,k} · e^{δ_{a*,d,k}} · [2 exp(δ_{a*,θ,k} + γ_{θ,k}·y_{a*}) - 1]^{-1}, marginalizing over cascade features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marginalize over empirical cascade-feature distribution f̂_ρ(x) as with popularity prediction; interpret half-life differences across classes and publishers for dynamics (fast/slow/usual diffusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation & Bayesian inference settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement BMH-P and BMH-K in Stan, use NUTS (Hamiltonian Monte Carlo) via CmdStanPy, employ non-centered parameterizations, and sample posterior with multiple chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper settings: 4 chains, adapt_delta = 0.9, 500 warmup iterations and 500 post-warmup iterations; use non-centered parametrization for normally distributed priors to speed convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation study design (feature/component variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess importance of item and cascade features and model components with ablated variants: (1) α(y) + z(x,y) (full), (2) α(y) + z(y) (no cascade features), (3) α(∅) + z(y) (no item effects in α), and (4) α(∅) + z(∅) (no features). Analogous ablations for θ/d and z in BMH-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit each variant per publisher and compare ARE / holdout log-likelihood to quantify the contribution of y_a and x_ac. Use these ablations to show whether seed-user or publisher-level signals dominate across publisher types (controversial vs reputable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterfactual headline-style profiling methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use trained publisher-level BMH-P/-K models to predict how articles with different headline styles (neutral, clickbait, inflammatory) would perform if published by each publisher, using an external HEADLINES dataset of labeled headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For counterfactuals where cascade features are unavailable, use item-only model variants (α(y) + z(y), θ(y) + z(y)). Predict expected cascade size (set Ĉ_ρ = 1 for heatmap visualization) and half-life, compute probability a headline is better-than-publisher-average, and visualize via performance heatmaps and contour plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation protocol and dataset splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Split CNIX and RNIX datasets into Fit (training) and Test (evaluation) periods with a one-month gap to ensure cascades in training are finished before test period: Fit = Jun 30, 2017 – Jan 1, 2019; Test = Feb 1, 2019 – Dec 31, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the temporal split and one-month gap to avoid leaking ongoing cascades; compute publisher-level empirical distributions (f̂_ρ(x), Ĉ_ρ) from Fit set and apply models to Test set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature engineering conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Article features: standardized 32-dimensional PCA-reduced all-MiniLM-L6-v2 headline embeddings as y_a. Cascade features: standardized log-follower count of seed user as x_ac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize features before modeling; reduce headline embeddings to manageable dimensionality (32-D) to trade-off expressivity and identifiability/regularization needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting & interpretation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report predictive performance using medians and 25th/75th quantiles; interpret differences across publisher groups (CNIX vs RNIX) to infer roles of seed-user popularity versus publisher reputation in cascade dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show both popularity (ARE) and temporal (NLL) comparisons; use ablation and counterfactual analyses to support substantive claims (e.g., clickbait effectiveness differs between controversial and reputable publishers).
